testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When starting from a stop, what should happen?

options.text: A vehicle should shift to the right.
A vehicle should be put into third gear.
A vehicle should not roll back.

questions.correctAnswerText: A vehicle should not roll back.
questions.explanation: Your vehicle should not roll backward when you start from a complete stop. This prevents hitting things behind you.

questions.question: Traction is important for:
questions.explanation: You need good traction to brake and steer your vehicle safely. Check your tires before every trip to make sure they are in good condition.

questions.question: In hot weather, tar spots bleeding on the pavement are:

options.text: Just as safe as the rest of the road.
Better for traction than the rest of the road.

questions.explanation: In very hot weather, tar rises to the road surface. These spots are very slippery. Watch for them and be careful.

questions.question: What must be shown on both sides of a commercial vehicle?
questions.explanation: Federal law requires the USDOT number to be displayed on both sides of each commercial vehicle.

questions.question: When loading a trailer, you should:

options.text: Put as little weight as possible over the axles.
Balance the weight evenly over the axles.
Put all weight directly over the axles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Balance the weight evenly over the axles.
questions.explanation: Load your cargo evenly. Too much weight on one axle can damage it and make steering harder. Too little weight on an axle reduces traction and makes handling difficult.

questions.question: Before backing up, you should:

options.text: Back up as fast as possible to finish quickly.
Walk your path and check for obstacles.
Use only the passenger side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk your path and check for obstacles.
questions.explanation: Before backing up, get out and walk the path you will take. Look for obstacles. Back up slowly and check both mirrors.

questions.question: A truck's weight affects:

options.text: Stopping distance less than the type of cargo.

questions.explanation: A vehicle's weight is very important for stopping distance. Heavier vehicles need more work from the brakes to stop completely.

questions.question: To prevent hydroplaning on wet roads:

options.text: Make sure your tires have good tread.
Let air out of your tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your tires have good tread.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens more often when tire pressure is too low or tread is worn. If you start to hydroplane, ease off the gas and push in the clutch to slow down.

questions.question: For normal braking power, a front brake limiting valve should be set to:
questions.explanation: Some vehicles have brake limiting valves with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Set it to "normal" for full braking power. The "slippery" setting reduces stopping power.

questions.question: When driving, you should:

options.text: Plan how to escape dangerous situations.
Turn your head all the way around instead of using mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan how to escape dangerous situations.
questions.explanation: Constantly watch the road for hazards. Think ahead about what you will do if these hazards become emergencies.

questions.question: Emergency equipment, such as fire extinguishers, is:

options.text: Only needed in vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Required in all commercial motor vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Required in all commercial motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must carry emergency equipment, including fire extinguishers.

questions.question: The ____ are turned on by an electric switch that the brake pedal activates.
questions.explanation: Brake lights turn on when you press the brake pedal. Air pressure activates an electric switch that turns on the brake lights.

questions.question: During an applied leakage test, the maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle is ____ per minute.
questions.explanation: A double combination vehicle should not lose more than 4 psi of air pressure per minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How quickly you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: During the driving test, the examiner scores you on your driving maneuvers and your general driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and signals, and avoid accidents and moving violations.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of driver fatigue?
questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include heavy eyelids, frequent blinking, yawning, trouble focusing, drifting from your lane, missing exits, and feeling restless. Feeling hungry is not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: An empty truck:

options.text: Stops in a shorter distance than a full truck.
Stops in a longer distance than a full truck.
Stops in the same distance as a full truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops in a longer distance than a full truck.
questions.explanation: Empty trucks need longer stopping distances than full trucks because they have less weight and less traction.

questions.question: When asked to make a turn during the driving test, you should:

options.text: Not use your turn signal since you were told to turn.
Check traffic only to your right.

questions.explanation: When making a turn during the driving test, check traffic in all directions and use your turn signal.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, a separate air tank can be used to:

options.text: Make the air brakes work more effectively.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A separate air tank can release the spring brakes for a short time if they have been applied due to low air pressure. This allows the driver to move the vehicle in an emergency.

questions.question: When starting an engine during a pre-trip inspection, the driver should:

options.text: Put the engine in first gear.

questions.explanation: After starting the engine during a pre-trip inspection, listen for any unusual noises.

questions.question: How long does it take for oil pressure to reach normal level when starting a vehicle?
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, oil pressure should reach a normal level within seconds. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or changing.

questions.question: What do ABS brakes do?

options.text: Stop your wheels from locking up.
Prevent your vehicle from speeding up on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop your wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: ABS (Anti-Lock Braking System) stops your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you slow down other drivers, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and block traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow it).

questions.question: What happens to a cargo van when you add weight?

options.text: It stays about the same height.
It gets taller with a heavy load.
It sits lower with a heavy load.

questions.correctAnswerText: It sits lower with a heavy load.
questions.explanation: A heavy load makes a vehicle sit lower than normal. A vehicle is taller when it is empty and shorter when it is fully loaded. If your vehicle fits under a low bridge when full, it might not fit when empty.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Always use it when changing lanes.
Only use it if another vehicle is next to you.
Do not use it if the lane change is obvious.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use it when changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?
questions.explanation: Get out of their way if possible. Do not make eye contact, as this can provoke them. Ignore what they do or say and do not respond.

questions.question: When driving down a steep hill, what should you use most to slow down?
questions.explanation: Use your engine to slow down on steep hills. Shift to a lower gear before going down the hill. Using only the brakes can cause them to overheat and fail.

questions.question: Is texting while driving allowed?

options.text: Yes, if you are texting your employer.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous and is never permitted.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver confronts you?
questions.explanation: Get out of their way if you can. Do not make eye contact. Ignore their hand gestures and do not respond.

questions.question: Which tire condition is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: Inspect your tires before each trip. Tire sizes must match. Tires must not have cuts, cracks, or other damage.

questions.question: What should you do with a cracked rim?

options.text: Move it to the dual tire position.

questions.explanation: Check your wheels and rims before driving. Wheels or rims that have been welded are not safe and must be replaced.

questions.question: How much steering wheel play is allowed?
questions.explanation: A steering wheel should move no more than 10 degrees. This equals about two inches of movement at the rim of a 20-inch wheel. Too much play makes steering difficult.

questions.question: What should you do if the low pressure warning light comes on while driving?

options.text: Stop where you are and park
Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible

questions.correctAnswerText: Exit the roadway as soon as safely possible
questions.explanation: When the low pressure warning light comes on, safely exit the roadway and park your vehicle as soon as you can. Low air pressure means your brakes will not work well enough to stop safely.

questions.question: What is true about a distracted driver?

options.text: Usually follows the rules of the road.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.explanation: Distracted drivers see dangers on the road more slowly than focused drivers. They may not see hazards at all.

questions.question: What happens if air tanks are not drained?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
Too much air collects in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air tanks must be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water is not removed, it can freeze in cold weather and cause brake failure.

questions.question: After changing a tire, what should you do a short distance later?

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
Make sure the tire is clean.
Add air to the new tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance later to check that all lug nuts are still tight.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs needed for a 10-foot load?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. However, all cargo must have at least two tie-downs, regardless of size.

questions.question: Is it legal to use a hand-held cell phone while driving?

options.text: Yes, if it is for work.

questions.explanation: Using a hand-held cell phone while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What should you NOT do at a railroad crossing during the driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle on the tracks if it is moving too slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During the driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.

questions.explanation: To avoid frustration that leads to aggressive driving, plan trips with realistic travel times to account for traffic delays. Other ways to prevent aggressive driving include driving at safe speeds, keeping proper following distance, avoiding hand gestures at other drivers, and keeping both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: Which is NOT a sign of bad brakes?

options.text: Pads free of oil or grease
Shoes covered with oil or grease

questions.correctAnswerText: Pads free of oil or grease
questions.explanation: When checking brakes, look for cracked drums, shoes or pads covered in oil, grease, or brake fluid, and shoes that are broken or dangerously thin. Clean pads are a sign of good brakes.

questions.question: When driving on a surface with poor traction, why should a driver accelerate slowly?

options.text: Because it is always good to accelerate slowly.
To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
So you do not accelerate faster than the vehicle ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep from losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Slow acceleration helps you keep control when driving in poor traction conditions, such as rain or snow.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a sign of fatigue?

options.text: Yawning repeatedly or rubbing your eyes

questions.explanation: Signs of fatigue include difficulty focusing, frequent blinking, yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering the last few miles, missing exits, drifting from your lane, and following too closely. Staying in your lane is normal driving behavior, not a sign of fatigue.

questions.question: On a slippery road, what should a driver do?

options.text: Make turns as quickly as possible.

questions.explanation: On slippery roads, drive slowly and smoothly. Make turns gently and do not pass other vehicles unless necessary.

questions.question: When completing an offset back/right parking maneuver, what should you do?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/right parking maneuver, pull straight forward first. Then back up to the right. Make sure your vehicle stays within the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: A slack adjuster should move no more than ____ from where it is attached to the push rod.
questions.explanation: Before each trip, pull the slack adjusters to check them. They should move no more than about one inch from where the push rod is attached. If they move more than one inch, they may need adjustment.

questions.question: When driving, how often should mirrors be used?

options.text: Only when there may be a problem.

questions.explanation: You need to know what is around your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors regularly while driving.

questions.question: What should be done with manual air tank drains?

options.text: Open them to drain the tanks after each day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open them to drain the tanks after each day.
questions.explanation: Compressed air in air brake systems contains water and compressor oil. These can damage brakes if they build up. Open manual air tank drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: Which of the following is required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or three liquid burning flares, and at least one fire extinguisher that is properly charged.

questions.question: When applying for a hazardous materials endorsement, which crime will disqualify you?
questions.explanation: A felony conviction for arson will disqualify you from getting, renewing, or transferring a hazardous materials endorsement.

questions.question: If you are not sure how to put out a fire in your vehicle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you are not sure which extinguisher to use, especially for a hazardous materials fire, wait for the firefighters to arrive and let them handle it.
